releases.notes:
I've updated LifeLink 1.0.1 for Minecraft **26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3**. One JAR covers this entire range. The gameplay and mod version stay the same.

## Download and install

Download **lifelink-1.0.1-mc26.jar** below. Requires **Java 25**, **Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer**, and **Fabric API built for your exact Minecraft version**.

Put LifeLink and Fabric API in the server's `mods` folder. Players don't need LifeLink installed to join a dedicated server. For singleplayer or LAN, install both mods locally. Install one LifeLink JAR at a time.

For Minecraft **1.21 through 1.21.11**, use the [1.21 build](https://github.com/adminvvv/LifeLink/releases/tag/v1.0.1).

## What's included

- Shared deaths, Spectator mode, and the original death title for joining and rejoining players.
- Settings and shared deaths saved across server restarts and LAN world reloads.
- Commands restricted to operator players or the world owner.
- Natural deaths enabled by default; PvP deaths enabled with `/lifelink pvpdeaths`.
- My LifeLink icon, MIT license and updated Java 25 build.

Both Minecraft builds share the round and saved-state logic to make future updates easier.

## Checks

The same 26.x JAR passed **17 automated checks on each of five releases: 85 checks total**, without dependency overrides. The shared-code update also passed **204 regression checks** across the twelve supported 1.21 releases.

These checks cover Fabric initialization and mocked server/player behavior. Live multiplayer testing of this 26.x build is still pending.

[Commands and setup](https://github.com/adminvvv/LifeLink/blob/v1.0.1-mc26/README.md) · [Compatibility results](https://github.com/adminvvv/LifeLink/blob/v1.0.1-mc26/mc26/compatibility/verified-results.json)

releases.notes:
I've updated LifeLink to support Minecraft 1.21 through 1.21.11 with one Fabric JAR.

## Changes

- Shared deaths and settings now survive server restarts and reopening LAN worlds.
- Joining and rejoining players stay dead while a shared death is active, with the original victim's message and title.
- All LifeLink commands require an operator player or the world owner.
- Natural deaths are enabled by default in new worlds. Use `/lifelink pvpdeaths` to enable PvP deaths.
- Existing saved death-toggle preferences are preserved.
- The LifeLink icon is included in the JAR.

## Install

Download **lifelink-1.0.1.jar** below. Requires **Java 21**, **Fabric Loader 0.18.4 or newer**, and **Fabric API built for your Minecraft version**.

For a dedicated server, put LifeLink and Fabric API in the server's `mods` folder. Players don't need LifeLink installed to join. For singleplayer or LAN, install both mods locally.

## Checks

The same release JAR passed 17 automated checks on each of the 12 supported Minecraft versions: **204 checks total**. I also tested live gameplay on 1.21 and 1.21.11 during development.

[Commands and setup](https://github.com/adminvvv/LifeLink/blob/v1.0.1/README.md) · [Compatibility results](https://github.com/adminvvv/LifeLink/blob/v1.0.1/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md)

mods.name: Life Link
mods.description: Hardcore mod that links deaths between players.

releases.notes:
**Overview**
LifeLink is a server-side Minecraft mod that links the lives of all players on a server. When one player dies, everyone dies! The mod was originally created for a private SMP and is perfect for cooperative or challenge-based gameplay.

**Features**
- **Shared lives**: All players' lives are linked—if one player dies, all players die.
- **Server-side only:** No client installation required; just add to your server's mods folder.
- **In-game commands:**
  - `/lifelink start` — Start the LifeLink challenge.
  - `/lifelink stop` — Stop the LifeLink challenge.
  - `/lifelink revive` — Revive all players.
  - `/lifelink naturaldeaths` — Enable or disable everyone dying from natural causes (e.g., falling, lava, etc.).
